title: Towards Microphone-Invariant Speech Representations for Transformer-Based Voice Disorder Detection
abstract: arXiv:2611.21140v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automatic voice disorder detection from speech offers strong potential for early diagnosis and continuous disease monitoring. While models based on pre-trained transformers have improved detection performance, their robustness to microphone variation remains underexplored, particularly for consumer-grade devices. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first study of microphone mismatch in transformer-based binary voice disorder detection across 20 smartphone microphones. While most mismatched microphone conditions cause moderate performance degradation, the worst-case condition reduces unweighted average recall by up to 12.53 percentage points. To address this, we introduce a Barlow Twins-inspired module to learn microphone-invariant representations. translated_title: 面向基于Transformer的嗓音障碍检测的麦克风不变语音表示研究
translated_abstract: 从语音中自动检测嗓音障碍为早期诊断和疾病的持续监测提供了巨大潜力。虽然基于预训练Transformer的模型提升了检测性能，但它们对麦克风变化的鲁棒性仍未得到充分探索，尤其是针对消费级设备。据我们所知，本研究首次在基于Transformer的二分类嗓音障碍检测中研究了跨20种智能手机麦克风的麦克风不匹配问题。虽然大多数不匹配的麦克风条件会导致中等程度的性能下降，但最坏情况会使非加权平均召回率降低多达12.53个百分点。为解决这一问题，我们引入了一个受Barlow Twins启发的模块来学习麦克风不变的语音表示。我们的方法将匹配与不匹配条件之间的性能差距缩小了多达62%，同时在匹配条件下保持了相当的检测性能。
tldr: 首次研究了Transformer嗓音障碍检测中跨20种智能手机麦克风的麦克风不匹配问题，并提出受Barlow Twins启发的模块学习麦克风不变表示，将匹配与不匹配条件间的性能差距缩小多达62%。
